title: How FOIA Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explain the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA): its origins in 1966 under Rep. John Moss and President Lyndon Johnson, the Watergate-era strengthening and Gerald Ford veto override, amendments under Reagan, Clinton, George W. Bush and Obama (including the 2016 FOIA Improvement Act and lobbying against it), how to file a request and appeal denials, the nine exemptions, the Glomar response from Philippi v. CIA, the Clinton email revelations, and Jason Leopold's FOIA work. The episode opens with vacation banter and closes with a listener mail about psychopathy.
topics: how to file a FOIA request

entities.name: Honest Leadership and Open Government Act

segments.title: Opening banter and Sunshine Week
segments.summary: Hosts open with vacation and hurricane-recovery banter, then introduce Sunshine Week and the idea of government openness.

segments.title: Origins of FOIA and Rep. John Moss
segments.summary: Government secrecy in the postwar era; Representative John Moss's requests denied; ASNE study; Cold War classification culture; Moss meets President Johnson, who is skeptical; the 1966 Freedom of Information Act passes the House and is signed quietly.

segments.title: Congressional support, scope, and Watergate-era strengthening
segments.summary: Congress's unanimous votes on FOIA; FOIA applies only to the executive branch; quote from journalist John Weiner on secrecy; post-Watergate amendments add sanctions and deadlines; Ford's veto is overridden on advice from Rumsfeld and Scalia.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Short ad break before the next segment.

segments.title: FOIA under Reagan, Clinton, and George W. Bush
segments.summary: Reagan tightens access and promotes classification; Clinton releases Cold War documents, digitizes records and extends response time to twenty days; George W. Bush restricts access after September 11 and limits former presidents' records, while expanding journalist fee status to bloggers and public interest groups.
topics: Honest Leadership and Open Government Act

segments.title: Obama memo and the 2016 FOIA Improvement Act
segments.summary: Obama's first-day memo promising transparency and a presumption of disclosure; Eric Holder's guidelines; FOIA requests reveal administration lobbying against codifying the disclosure presumption; a 2014 House bill passes unanimously but dies; the 2016 FOIA Improvement Act; use of the Espionage Act against sources.

segments.title: How to file a FOIA request
segments.summary: Who can file, fees and journalist status, finding each agency's FOIA office, the timeline of twenty days, appeals and federal court, and tips such as being courteous, succinct and specific, and checking whether records already exist.

segments.title: The nine FOIA exemptions and the editor's obligation
segments.summary: Walkthrough of the nine exemptions including national security, personnel rules, trade secrets, the deliberative 'opinion' exemption (most used), privacy, law enforcement, financial regulators, and geological data; a journalist argues editors should report stonewalling.

segments.title: Landmark cases: Glomar response and Clinton emails
segments.summary: Philippi v. CIA origin of the Glomar response over the Hughes-built Glomar Explorer; the 2016 appeals ruling on personal email accounts; the Clinton email server revealed through FOIA requests including by Jason Leopold; the cost barrier to lawsuits.

segments.title: Listener mail on psychopathy
segments.summary: A listener writes about being a high-functioning psychopath and the hosts react briefly.

segments.title: Outro and contact info
segments.summary: Hosts thank the listener and give social media and email contact information.
